newsitem.title: USA: N.Y comptroller urges hiking state pensions - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.Y comptroller urges hiking state pensions - paper.

text.p: The New York state comptroller plans to propose a bill to give public retirees regular rises in their pensions, provided the pension fund performs better than expected, the Albany Times Union said on Thursday.

The legislature has balked at the cost of pension increases, and the comptroller's new plan represents a compromise, as it would allow the state to pay for the increases without having to set aside funds in the budget.

The paper quoted the president of the Retired Public Employees Association, Cynthia Wilson, as saying the comptroller's plan calls for measuring whether the state fund performs better or worse than a standard index.

Any extra funds would go toward reducing employer contributions for the next year, and some would go toward a cost of living adjustment for retirees. The comptroller announced his proposal at the association's annual meeting this week, the paper said.
It added that in the 1996 fiscal year, the New York State and Local Retirement System earned a 21.8 percent return.
